title: L-FAME: Longitudinal Focused Attention Meditation EEG Dataset and Benchmark
claim: A multi-stage study protocol and standardized task sequence define how longitudinal data is collected, making the resource reproducible.
layout: Flow left-to-right in four phases, then a bottom row of task boxes
description: A flowchart of the study protocol. The top row runs left to right. A group of illustrated students labeled 'Participants Recruited' leads to a clipboard 'Screening' icon and 'Included Participants (novices)'. Next come four colored panels: a blue Pre-Intervention (Baseline) box with consent, video demonstration, practice schedule, verification, baseline EEG recording and questionnaires; a green 6-Week Training Period box with a week timeline, a practice schedule (5, 10 and 15 min/day), a daily journal and a mid-intervention check-in; and a purple Post-Intervention box with the repeat EEG recording and questionnaires. Arrows from the baseline and post boxes feed a bottom 'EEG Session Task Sequence' strip of five rounded boxes: RestOE, RestCE01, Medita, RestCE02 and SLMedita. Each box has a brain, thought-cloud or meditating-figure icon and a duration. Pastel colors separate the phases, and the eye starts at the participants on the left.

abstract: We introduce a novel Longitudinal Focused Attention Meditation Electroencephalography (L-FAME) dataset and an accompanying benchmark, designed to foster research into the neural effects of various meditation practices and the evolution of these effects over a six-week training period. The dataset includes baseline EEG recordings from 74 healthy college participants, of whom 44 completed the six-week intervention and returned for post-intervention recordings, along with psychological assessments. Participants were randomly assigned to one of three distinct meditation groups: two mantra-based techniques (SA-TA-NA-MA and Hare Krishna) and one Breath Focus practice. Leveraging this unique longitudinal and comparative dataset, we propose a benchmark suite comprising three distinct classification tasks: (1) cognitive state decoding to distinguish between resting and meditation states, (2) fine-grained classification of the specific meditation techniques, and (3) cross-session adaptation to evaluate model generalization across the longitudinal time gap. We provide comprehensive baseline results for these tasks utilizing a range of classical machine learning algorithms and deep learning architectures. The complete dataset, preprocessing pipelines, and benchmark evaluation code are being publicly released, offering a valuable resource and a standardized framework for the development and comparison of new analytical methods in computational meditation research and EEG-based machine learning. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/L-FAME-Dataset-Benchmark/L-FAME
